great: {owner}: 'Brilliant week, {name}. Guests keep asking for you by name.'
{owner}: 'Honestly? Best week you've had. Keep this up and we'll be talking about {nextRung} soon.'
{owner}: 'You made the whole team better this week. Thank you.'
good: {owner}: 'Solid week. Turned up, worked hard, kept smiling. That's the job.'
{owner}: 'Good stuff, {name}. A couple of slow moments, but I'm happy.'
{owner}: 'Nice and steady. Steady is how restaurants survive.'
ok: {owner}: 'An okay week. Let's pick one thing to get better at next week.'
{owner}: 'Not bad, not your best. Get some rest on your day off.'
{owner}: 'You were a bit slow on Friday. Everyone has those nights.'
poor: {owner}: 'Tough week. Is everything alright? Let's have a proper chat.'
{owner}: 'I need more from you, {name}. I know you can do it.'
{owner}: 'Missed shifts hurt the team. Can we sort the rota out together?'

great: {owner}: 'Great week. Don't let it go to your head, mind; I'm not made of money.'
{owner}: 'Good work. You saved us a fortune in wasted stock. That's what I like to see.'
{owner}: 'Top marks. If everyone worked like you, I could switch the heating back on.'
good: {owner}: 'Fine week. You didn't break anything, which is a bonus.'
{owner}: 'Decent. Use less kitchen roll and we'll call it excellent.'
ok: {owner}: 'Meh. Plates went out, money came in. Just about.'
{owner}: 'Try to be quicker. Time is money, and I like money.'
{owner}: 'Average week. Average is cheap, at least.'
poor: {owner}: 'Bad week. Wasted food, wasted time. Do better or I'll have to rethink the rota.'
{owner}: 'I counted the drops. Then I counted them again. Please, {name}.'
{owner}: 'We can't afford weeks like this. Let's both try harder.'

great: {owner}: 'Exceptional, {name}. That's the standard this restaurant was built for.'
{owner}: 'The guests noticed. So did I. Beautiful work.'
{owner}: 'You were the calmest person in the building on Saturday. That's leadership.'
good: {owner}: 'Good week. Now let's make it a great one: details, details, details.'
{owner}: 'Well done. Your plating is getting sharper every week.'
{owner}: 'Strong. Keep pushing and you'll be ready for {nextRung}.'
ok: {owner}: 'Acceptable, but our guests expect more than acceptable.'
{owner}: 'A few plates weren't quite right. Take your time; get it perfect.'
{owner}: 'You're better than this week. Let's prove it.'
poor: {owner}: 'That wasn't up to standard, {name}. We need to talk about it.'
{owner}: 'Two plates came back this week. In this kitchen, that's two too many.'
{owner}: 'I believe in you. But I need to see it on the plate.'

chef_de_partie.title: Chef de partie
chef_de_partie.copy: Run your own section of the kitchen, like the grill or the sauces. You'll need good knife skills, plenty of shifts and a happy owner.

sous_chef.title: Sous chef
sous_chef.copy: Second in command. When the head chef is off, the kitchen is yours. Show you can cook every station and keep calm in a rush.

head_chef.title: Head chef
head_chef.copy: The top job: you write the menu and run the pass. You'll need real skill, a strong reputation and the owner's full trust.

bartender.title: Bartender
bartender.copy: Mix the drinks, not just carry the glasses. Learn the recipes and be quick and friendly with guests.

bar_manager.title: Bar manager
bar_manager.copy: Order the stock, train the team and keep the bar tidy and profitable. Skill and charm both count.

general_manager.title: General manager
general_manager.copy: Run the whole restaurant, front and back. The owner has to trust you with the keys.

head_waiter.title: Head waiter
head_waiter.copy: Lead the floor team, look after the trickiest tables and keep the smiles coming. Charm matters most.

restaurant_manager.title: Restaurant manager
restaurant_manager.copy: Run the dining room: rotas, bookings and happy guests. You'll need a good reputation and great reviews.

general_manager.title: General manager
general_manager.copy: Take charge of the whole business, from the bank balance to the bin rota. Keep the numbers and the team healthy.

partner.title: Partner (equity)
partner.copy: The owner offers you a slice of the restaurant itself. Earn it with steady profits, a strong reputation and their complete confidence.

granted: {owner}: 'Congratulations, {name}. You're our new {rung}. Your wage goes up to {wage}.'
Big news: {name} is now {rung}! The team clapped. Someone made a cake (it was slightly burnt).
notYet: {owner}: 'Not yet, {name}. Look at the checklist: you're close.'
{owner}: 'I love the ambition. Give it a few more weeks.'
promotion.givenToSomeoneElse: {owner} gave the {nextRung} job to someone else this time. It's disappointing, but there will be another chance.
promotion.topRung: You're at the top of the ladder here. The next step is a big one: your own place.

mentor.offer: {mentor} has offered to show you the ropes. A good mentor makes everything easier.
chef: {mentor}: 'Taste everything. Twice. Then taste it again.'
{mentor}: 'A sharp knife is a safe knife. Look after it and it looks after you.'
{mentor}: 'Clean as you go. A messy station means a messy plate.'
{mentor}: 'Everyone burns things. Good chefs just start again faster.'
bar: {mentor}: 'Know your stock. Running out of lemons on a Friday is a disaster.'
{mentor}: 'Measure everything. Guessing is how you lose money and friends.'
waiter: {mentor}: 'Look at the table, not at your notepad. People want to feel seen.'
{mentor}: 'Carry two plates well before you try three.'
{mentor}: 'If something goes wrong, say sorry and fix it. Never argue.'
manager: {mentor}: 'Check the numbers every night. Little leaks sink big ships.'
{mentor}: 'Look after your team and they'll look after your guests.'
{mentor}: 'Never make a rota when you're tired.'
mentor.session: You spent an hour with {mentor}. You feel a bit more confident.
mentor.busy: {mentor} is too busy today. Try again tomorrow.

balanced: {owner} at {rival}: 'I've heard good things. Come and be our {rung} for {wage}.'
{rival} is growing and needs a {rung}. {owner} says you're top of their list.
cheap: {owner} at {rival}: 'We're busy, cheerful and we need a {rung}. The pay's {wage}. The staff meal is chips.'
{rival} is looking for a {rung}. 'No fuss, lots of customers,' says {owner}.
premium: {owner} at {rival}: 'We only hire the best. We think that might be you. {rung}, {wage}.'
{rival}, the smart place in town, wants you as {rung}. The kitchen has copper pans.

offers.accepted: You've accepted the job at {rival}. Your new team is excited to meet you.
offers.declined: You politely said no to {rival}. They said the door is always open.
offers.expired: The offer from {rival} has run out.

granted: {owner}: 'You've earned it. Your wage goes up by {raise} an hour.'
{owner} thinks for a moment, then nods. 'Fair's fair. {raise} more an hour from next week.'
small: {owner}: 'I can't do much, but here's {raise} an hour more. I hope that helps.'
refused: {owner}: 'Not right now, {name}. Money's tight this month. Ask me again in a few weeks.'
{owner}: 'Show me a few more great weeks and we'll talk.'
annoyed: {owner}: 'You asked me last week! Give it time.'
raise.matchedOffer: {owner}: 'I don't want to lose you. I'll match {rival}'s offer.'

openOwnPlace.ready: You've saved {savings} and learned a lot. Time to open your own place?
openOwnPlace.notReady: Not yet: you need more savings or more experience before the bank will help.
farewell: {owner}: 'I always knew you'd leave one day. I'm proud of you, {name}. Go and be brilliant.'
Your last shift at {restaurant}. The team signs a tea towel for you. It says 'Don't forget us!'
handover: The keys are yours. It's your name over the door now.
You bring {savings} of savings, everything you learned in {shifts} shifts, and a few friends who'd love to work for you.
From today, you're the owner. Hire your team, write your menu and open your doors. Good luck, chef!

perks.skills: Your skills come with you: you cook (or serve) like the {rung} you were.
perks.friends: Old friends from {restaurant} want to join your team.
perks.regulars: A few regulars follow you to the new place.
perks.savings: Your savings of {savings} go into the business.
perks.reputation: People in the trade know your name already.
